panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph (panel A) showing extensive spontaneous ecchymosis over the left hip and upper thigh. The caption and in-text explicitly attribute this to soft-tissue extravasation from an underlying spontaneous iliopsoas hemorrhage in acquired hemophilia A, a real patient, untreated disease manifestation. This is a classic spontaneous soft-tissue/muscle bleed presentation of hemophilia A. The visible skin is light and adequately lit; no ethnicity or age is stated, so those fields are null/unknown.

in_text_mentions: Ultrasonography of the left groin demonstrated a subfascial hematoma within the iliopsoas muscle without evidence of an inguinal or femoral hernia or hip joint effusion. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen and pelvis confirmed a large spontaneous hematoma involving the left iliopsoas muscle. During hospitalization, the patient developed extensive spontaneous ecchymosis involving the left hip and upper thigh secondary to soft tissue extravasation from the underlying hemorrhage (Figure 1).

panels.rationale: Single axial contrast-enhanced CT angiography image from a real patient (no third-party restriction noted). The panel shows a large left-sided iliopsoas hematoma with focal arterial contrast extravasation (asterisk) indicating active hemorrhage. Combined with the disease-focused article title ('Acquired Groin Pain Revealing Acquired Hemophilia A: A Case Report of Spontaneous Iliopsoas Hematoma') and the in-text mention of 'active arterial contrast extravasation within the iliacus muscle, consistent with ongoing bleeding', this is a specific spontaneous intramuscular bleeding manifestation of hemophilia A. panels.rationale: Axial MRI of the right thigh with arrows indicating a real human-patient manifestation of hemophilia A. Disease attribution is strong and panel-specific: the article title and in-text state acquired hemophilia A (factor VIII 2%, prolonged uncorrected aPTT with normal PT/INR) and intramuscular bleeding into the anterior right thigh, matching the configured target hemophilia_a. The imaged manifestation (rectus femoris hemorrhage/intramuscular bleed) maps to the vocabulary finding hemophilia_a_intramuscular_hematoma; the accompanying compartment edema is not in the vocabulary and is listed as a proposed finding. No panel letters are present, so the unlabeled single figure is treated as panel A. Intramuscular hematoma is a recognized but less common bleeding site than hemarthrosis and is described as suspected hemorrhage without an organized collection, hence variant. No age, ethnicity, or assessable skin is shown (MRI). [raw subtype: acquired]
